column1: # The numbers in the story and who first reported each: one row per number, 19 rows, made on Nov 25, 2026 from the saved pages. For each: what it counts; the first report found among the saved pages (outlet, date, on whose word, saved id); later reports and how they changed the number; saved pages that contradict a first reporter or a date given in the argument or in the project's ledger of numbers; a note. Quotations were checked against the saved copies by script. "First" means first among the pages the project holds, not first in the world. One number of the working list is left out here (Singapore's export growth in October 2026): its only source was a release on a site whose robots file bars scripted access, and the project does not cite copies taken from such sites.

column2: Nvidia chips (H200s) stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to the mainland
column3: Reuters, Nov 5, 2026 (its own dateline, as Yahoo's copy prints it [cn-clips-reuters-hongkong-yahoo]; the copy quoted here is CNA's, dated Nov 6), two unnamed people: "About 600,000 of Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips are stored in Hong Kong" [cn-clips-evidence-1]
column4: Reuters repeats it on Nov 18, 2026 as H200s: "around 600,000 H200 chips were being stored in Hong Kong" [cn-acts-reuters-halt-20261118-relay2]; relays only (Data Center Dynamics, DigiTimes); the foreign ministry, asked on Nov 9, referred the question on; Luckey's clip of Nov 19 gives the same figure without a source. No revision.

column2: H200 chips Chinese companies ordered for 2026
column3: Reuters, Dec 31, 2025, two people: "Chinese technology companies have placed orders for more than 2 million H200 chips for 2026" [cn-labs-h200-two-million-202512-relay1-wayback]
column4: Not revised. Lianhe Zaobao repeats it as hearsay on Jan 28, 2026 [cn-cnpress-zaobao-h200-conditions-20260128]. Set against it on the record: Nvidia's chief executive, Jan 29, 2026, "we have not received purchase orders" [cn-ga31-inte-scmp-h200-approvals-20260128-wayback] (Voice of America's Chinese rendering has not yet: "我们尚未收到采购订单" [cn-ga31-counter-40]); Mar 17, 2026, orders "from many customers" (no number) [cn-le10-huang-restart-20260318-fmt-afp]; the Treasury Secretary, Nov 20, 2026, "a paucity of orders" [cn-against2-bessent-orders-20261120].
column6: Orders here may not be purchase orders placed with Nvidia (a caution from the search for evidence against).

column6: Stock wherever held; not the Hong Kong count.

column2: H200s (with AMD's MI325 counted in) Washington would let each Chinese buyer have
column3: Bloomberg, Mar 3, 2026 (on the Los Angeles Times), people familiar, as a cap under discussion: "limiting Chinese firms to buying 75,000 of Nvidia’s H200 chips each" [cn-ga31-numbers-42]
column4: Reuters, May 14, 2026, two people: "each approved customer can purchase up to 75,000 chips" [cn-acts-reuters-us-approvals-20260514-wayback]; Washington's table of May 11, 2026 (published Nov 19): no approved application above 75,000, and 75,000 Nvidia plus 75,000 AMD for each of the ByteDance and Tencent groups [cn-usdocs-hfac-decisions-20261119]; the FT, August 2026, gives "up to 100,000" each [cn-tolerate-reutersaug26-relay1-wayback]: no report says the cap was raised.
column5: The project's ledger of numbers gave, when this table was made, the 75,000 from Reuters, May 14, 2026; Bloomberg reported it on Mar 3, 2026.
column6: Bloomberg also: the cap was less than half of what Alibaba and ByteDance had told Nvidia they wanted.
